content.value_statement: Large configuration files and repeated context increase token usage. This skill reviews Caveman reports and applies measured changes with individual approval.
actual_capabilities: Runs the Caveman learn report and presents ranked token sinks.
Distinguishes reducible, recurring-context, and load-bearing findings.
Previews configuration edits and requests approval for each change.
Offloads verified recurring context into cavemem with a recall pointer.
Measures token usage after changes and reverts ineffective edits.
Confirms recall and recovery paths before completing an offload.
limitations: Requires Caveman commands and a compatible report.
Changes only findings selected and approved by the user.
Reports inferred token savings without currency estimates.

use_cases.title: Trim project instructions
use_cases.description: Review a large CLAUDE.md and approve only edits that reduce measured tokens per turn.

use_cases.title: Offload recurring context
use_cases.description: Move repeated session context into cavemem while preserving compact recall and exact recovery paths.

use_cases.title: Review team token usage
use_cases.description: Present ranked token sinks and separate actionable configuration findings from load-bearing context.

prompt_templates.title: Review my report
prompt_templates.prompt: Run my Caveman learn report and explain the ranked token sinks without changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce configuration tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Review reducible findings, show each proposed diff and measured impact, then ask before every edit.

prompt_templates.title: Offload repeated context
prompt_templates.prompt: Find recurring context suitable for cavemem, verify its hash, measure recall cost, and propose a reversible offload.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize selected findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Process only my selected sinks, preserve load-bearing content, validate every recall path, and revert changes without confirmed token reduction.

output_examples.input: Review my report without editing anything.
output_examples.output: Cave Score: 72. The largest reducible sink is project instructions. Recurring context ranks second. Load-bearing guidance remains unchanged.

output_examples.input: Propose a safe offload for the repeated deployment notes.
output: Source hash matches the report locator.
The compact pointer and recall cost are lower than repeated loading.
Approve storing the block and replacing it with the proposed recall pointer?

output_examples.output: The approved section was trimmed. Tokens per turn decreased from 420 to 285. The original content and reversal steps are recorded.

best_practices: Review the complete report before selecting changes.
Approve each diff only after checking its measured impact.
Test recall and exact recovery before accepting an offload.
anti_patterns: Do not apply every recommendation without reviewing individual diffs.
Do not remove load-bearing instructions to improve the score.
Do not keep changes that fail to reduce tokens or preserve recall.

faq.question: Does this skill edit files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It requests explicit approval before each file change.

faq.question: What is a reducible finding?
faq.answer: It is configuration content that can be shortened while preserving required agent behavior.

faq.question: What is recurring context?
faq.answer: It is information repeatedly loaded or pasted across sessions that may be stored for compact recall.

faq.question: How does cavemem offloading stay reversible?
faq.answer: The workflow keeps a recall pointer, supports exact recovery, and records source restoration steps.

faq.question: Will it change load-bearing content?
faq.answer: No. Load-bearing findings are displayed for accurate scoring but remain untouched.

faq.question: How are savings validated?
faq.answer: The skill compares tokens per turn before and after each change and reverts changes without a reduction.
